learning_objective: 🎯 Follow the magical journey of a cotton shirt from a farmer's field all the way to your closet by learning about economic activities!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Primary activities mean working directly with nature to get raw materials. Farming crops, catching fish in the sea, and digging for minerals are all primary activities!
We cannot wear raw cotton fluff! Secondary activities happen in factories where raw materials are changed into useful goods, like turning cotton into soft cloth or turning wood into a sturdy desk.
Tertiary activities are services that help people and businesses. Teachers, doctors, bus drivers, and shopkeepers do not make physical goods, but their services keep the world running smoothly!

fun_activity.title: 🍞 The Journey of Bread
fun_activity.instructions: Next time you eat a sandwich, try to list the three steps: The farmer growing the wheat (Primary), the baker baking the bread (Secondary), and the shopkeeper selling it to you (Tertiary)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Economic activities are things people do to earn a living and provide what society needs.
⭐ The primary sector extracts things from nature, like farming and mining.
⭐ The secondary sector manufactures raw materials into finished goods, and the tertiary sector provides helpful services.
